calls.reason: No named buyer has a documented NVIDIA-specific spending cut. Tesla's AI budget cut isn't split by supplier and coincided with oil and Meta news, so the antecedent and any market effect remain unestablished.
Evidence is one Replit database-deletion incident and a supervised-use slowdown study; neither measures how often unchecked agents break things or create net work, and 'not intelligent' is undefined.

Apollo's concentration data and NVIDIA's customer-concentration filing show vulnerability, but nothing measures market dependence on the buyers' purchases, chip losses, or a historical ranking; largely rhetorical.
'Never' has no deadline. Anthropic's self-report of agents taking over team work is company evidence, and its labor study found no clear unemployment effects, so neither side is settled.
Reports of 2024 losses and cost reclassification hint at weak economics, but no target-quarter financials or costed plan show whether a route to profit existed.
Amazon's filings show company-wide capex of only $3.4-4.9bn a year in 2012-2014. AWS is a subset of that, so even ten inflation-adjusted years falls below Amazon's $77.7bn of capex in 2024.
